chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from ['Ali ibn Harun] from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Choose the Rabiyyah pigeons for your houses, for indeed they curse the killers of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الرَّاعِبِيَّةَ: A specific breed or type of pigeon named Rabiyyah

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of keeping Rabiyyah pigeons in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Shia practice of attributing spiritual awareness to animals, specifically the Rabiyyah pigeon, which is believed to instinctively curse the killers of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). It underscores the concept of *al-Ghaybah al-Sughra* (minor occultation) era traditions where domestic life was infused with commemoration of Karbala, reinforcing the enduring enmity between the Ahl al-Bayt and their enemies. The specific breed's name, 'Rabiyyah,' may also allude to the tribe of Rabi'ah or denote a distinctive characteristic, linking the physical act of keeping pigeons to the metaphysical reality of divine retribution.
